newsitem.title: USA: FOCUS-Analysts skeptical over API "demand" figures.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Analysts skeptical over API "demand" figures.

text.p: The "implied demand" for gasoline in the U.S. was at a near-record pace if the latest American Petroleum Institute (API) weekly status report is to be believed, though oil analysts were highly skeptical.

"It's not true demand, just inventory movement," said John Saucer, a Houston-based oil analyst for Smith Barney. And the Department of Energy's figures, showing year-to-date gasoline demand barely changed, have been "underwhelming" so far this year.
In the API report, gasoline "implied demand" was running at 8.76 million barrels a day last week.
Gasoline inventories are closely watched in the run-up to the Memorial Day weekend and the start of "driving season" in the U.S., when gasoline demand is at its seasonal highest.

The combination of stocks drawdown (3.6 million bbls), output (7.768 million barrels per day-bpd) and imports (473,000 bpd) are added to get an "implied demand" figure, or guage on demand, analyst said.

"But I'm hesitant to put a lot of faith (in the API number), said Rich Redash, an analyst at Prudential Securities in New York. The 8.76 million bpd would be near record levels "and that's just hard to believe."
